episode

Benjamin Swift Reported on Chinese Miners in the Bolivian Amazon
For
The Guardian
, Benjamin Swift "spent five days with Chinese miners, investors and traders in Mayaya, Bolivia.” He said this was “the first time that the lives of Chinese gold prospectors in the Amazon have been documented in detail." Swift told
Study Hall
, "Mayaya is a small town that in recent years has become a hub for Chinese mining operating outside Bolivian law. The gold miners, investors, and importers welcomed us into their homes, where they told us everything about their operations in Bolivia – and how they got there."
Adam Robb Tracked Down Mario Batali in Michigan
For
Caper
, Adam Robb traveled "to Michigan, to the Traverse City Food and Wine Festival, to interview the infamous chef Mario Batali about his recent inroads toward making a comeback years after his sex scandal."
Robb told
Study Hall: "
After my plans to attend his lunch event and interview him were canceled right before I arrived, I spent the weekend interviewing so many food celebrities in attendance, from Ruth Reichl to Andrew Zimmern, about whether Batali deserves to be redeemed. Finally, fate led Batali and I right to one other on my last morning in town. Along the way I also learned he was never a recluse in Traverse City, but instead become a local celebrity on rock radio even at the height of his civil and criminal investigations."
Andrea Cooper Wrote About The "Jewish Inspired" Farming Tradition
For
The Guardian
, Andrea Cooper explored "the growing number of Jewish people in the U.S. who are seeking purpose and community through farming."
